objective: The hot loop of Quantizer8bitDirect<SIMDLevel 0>::encode_vector is a fully scalar, per-element float->uint8 precision conversion (code[i]=(uint8_t)x[i]) — flw, fcvt.wu.s rtz, sb per lane with 100% of samples at the scalar byte store — containing zero v* instructions even though libfaiss.so is built with V (v1p0, zve64d, zvl128b); because the operation is lane-independent and cache-friendly, the workload cost is the scalar loop body and loop control, not memory, and the leverage point is an RVV precision-conversion formulation (vle32 + vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v + truncating narrowing + vse8).

changes.rationale: Add an RVV precision-conversion fast path to Quantizer8bitDirect::encode_vector (or make the existing V-capable build actually emit vector code for this template): a dynamic-vsetvl strip-mined loop that unit-stride loads x with vle32, converts f32->u32 with vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v (same round-toward-zero semantics as the current scalar fcvt.wu.s rtz), truncates to 8-bit via a narrowing shift vnsrl.wi shift 0 so the stored byte equals the (uint8_t)x[i] truncation of the conversion result, and stores with vse8; keep the scalar loop as the fallback and unchanged codec contract, with scalar tail handling for partial vl.
instructions: Hardware and the libfaiss.so build expose standard V (v1p0, zve64d, zvl128b, VLEN=128).
d is large enough for vectorization to clear vsetvl/dispatch and tail costs (crossover measured on target).
(uint8_t)x[i] conversion semantics (fcvt.wu.s rtz then byte truncation) are preserved for every call input.
